ownership_and_late_data.closers: File handles use CloseHandle, search handles FindClose. Reserve once before invocation, including false/unknown/late returns. Known close success survives wrapper failure; no adapter destructor, portable finally, bootstrap finally or engine finally repeats it. Never guess a handle from an unobserved return.
ownership_and_late_data.primary: Keep any already latched Python primary object/phase unchanged. Later binding/copy/log/close errors are secondary. Raw API false/error facts remain independently retained even if a wrapper exception is the first Python exception; do not invent an earlier allocated PortError or silently reorder exception precedence.
ownership_and_late_data.read_buffer: The owner record retains the preallocated output-buffer reference and known returned slice/count before any copy/clock can throw. Do not reuse that storage until immutable capture is safely committed or the failed operation is retained. Known late bytes may remain unhashed/uncaptured; no positive file pin or renewed work after cutoff.
ownership_and_late_data.write_buffer: Retain the immutable prepared record and chunk before dispatch. A known short write advances only its count; do not retry an uncertain write or rehash/flush unknown tails into a positive pin. Returned flush/close flags are separate from output hash completeness.

proposed_boundary.counter_commit: Raw-record scalar-return fact is counted once by call ordinal. Portable return acknowledgment is a different counter, not a second native return. If counter formatting/allocation fails after raw adoption, derive known returns from the retained flags without replaying the API or clearing the known effect.
proposed_boundary.defined_count: Only the exact existing function-specific success+defined-count+range predicate advances known bytes. Raw zero with a defined successful count is a known zero; false/undefined/unreturned never becomes a known zero. Raw fields and definedness remain separate.
proposed_boundary.first_Python_visible_return: Immediately retain the raw scalar in the preallocated record and transfer usable handle/namespace/close status to the SAME actionable registry. Then retain count/definedness from preallocated outputs as each becomes observable. Do this before RawReturn allocation, error-string/last-error copy, post-call clock, query, log, hash or byte copy.
proposed_boundary.partial_Python_adoption: A scalar can be retained while count/error/buffer conversion remains unknown. Preserve each observed fact and pending field independently; a later wrapper exception never overwrites a known handle/flag/count as unknown. No retry of an uncertain invocation.
proposed_boundary.reservation: Before dispatch, reserve one owner+Origin+nonce+slot+call ordinal record and any C out-buffer, immutable write slice, expected capacity and closer class. Bound all records/buffers by the eventual jointly admitted plan. Reservation is not proof that C was entered.
proposed_boundary.residual_FFI_gap: Python-visible assignment is not atomic with native return or ctypes conversion. Async interruption/allocation/conversion before the first adoption can still leave an unknown side effect/handle. Preallocation narrows the window; it does not prove its absence. Any stronger C-level guarantee would require its own separately authorized design/build, not a claim from these Python/fake interfaces.
proposed_boundary.return_axes: Keep portable_call_reserved/entered, FFI_invocation_reserved, scalar_return_observed, count_observed/defined, and portable_wrapper_return_observed separately. Scalar-observed plus wrapper-exception means known raw return/effect and unknown or failed wrapper handoff, not an unreturned C call. Conversely ctypes argument/result conversion may prevent observing C entry/return: label that unknown rather than pretending a measured C census.
proposed_boundary.views: A source-issued adopted-return view may be allocated later, but it owns no handle and grants no new close right. It references the current record identity/owner/nonce. No dict, identity_ok flag, serialized receipt or HarnessIdentityPrecondition can stand in for raw adoption.
